name: JulSwap JulProtocolV2 addBNB spot-reserve quote treasury drain
summary: JulProtocolV2.addBNB() sized the protocol's own JULb contribution from the instantaneous WBNB/JULb reserve ratio and added it as liquidity with amountBNBMin = 1. Attackers crashed the JULb price with flash-swapped JULb, called addBNB so the treasury poured JULb into the pair at the crashed ratio, then bought JULb back cheaply and kept the BNB.
notes: Victims are JulProtocolV2 and the WBNB/JULb pair it supplies, netted per transaction: their BNB loss equals what each exploiter kept. The attacker's own earlier addBNB call 0xf2a37ce0 was an unmanipulated deposit, not an exploit.

JULb has no price and its only venue was crashed by the attack; the JULb that left the victims went to flash-swap repayment and fees, whose proceeds are already in the BNB, so it is listed at 0 USD (rule 15).
Contract-originated addBNB calls from 2026 by 0xc2182000 lost BNB for their sender and are not counted as exploits.
